question: Does `user-invocable: false` next to `disable-model-invocation: true` hide a skill from the slash menu, for plugin skills and project skills, and what happens when the hidden command is typed?
procedure: fresh git repo holding the project skills; the plugin loaded with --plugin-dir
claude -p "Reply with the single word OK." --plugin-dir <plugin> --output-format stream-json --verbose --model haiku --max-turns 1 — read slash_commands and skills from the init event
claude -p "/local-hidden say the marker" --output-format stream-json --verbose --model haiku --max-turns 2 < /dev/null — read the result event

observations.typedHiddenCommand: result success with num_turns 0 and total_cost_usd 0 — no model request was made and nothing ran

documentation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md — user-invocable: false hides a skill from the / menu
conclusion: The flag pair hides the skill from the menu in both plugin and project scope. A typed hidden command in print mode is dropped without an error, so a repo-mode eval that enters an internal skill by slash would run nothing and look like an empty pass. Internal-unit evals must enter by reading the SKILL.md, as the orchestrator does. Re-run this probe when Claude Code changes slash-command handling.
